title: Alia Bhatt and Sharvari Burn Down the Boys' Club. 'Alpha' Is the First Woman-Led YRF Spy Universe Film — and the Trailer Is Already No. 1.
excerpt: Hrithik Roshan's blink-and-miss cameo confirms the crossover, Bobby Deol plays the mentor she has to destroy, and one line — 'Sita aaj Lanka khud jalane aayi hai' — has the internet on fire. In theatres July 3.
body:
The trailer opens on a little girl, and the first thing her father teaches her is how to kill. By the time Alpha cuts to its title card, that girl has grown into Alia Bhatt in an avatar no one quite saw coming — scarred, feral, and entirely done asking permission. Three days after it dropped, the trailer was sitting at No. 1 on trending, and the internet had picked its side: this is the YRF Spy Universe's first film built around women, and it walked in swinging.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=QRqGwGwo1Y0

For a franchise that gave us Tiger, Pathaan and War — all of them muscled-up men jumping off things in slow motion — handing the keys to two women is the boldest swerve Yash Raj Films has made in a decade. And the trailer knows it. Bhatt plays Sita, a girl raised and weaponised by her adoptive father Fateh Singh Lakhawat (Bobby Deol, continuing the most convincing late-career renaissance in Hindi cinema). The "Alpha" program that built her turns out to be a nest of betrayal, and Sita goes rogue against the very system that made her. Then comes the line already echoing across every timeline: "Sita aaj Lanka khud jalane aayi hai." Sita has come to burn Lanka down herself. It lands like a thesis statement.

!Spy Universe — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

*"Then comes the line already echoing across every timeline: "Sita aaj Lanka khud jalane aayi hai." Sita has come to burn Lanka down herself."*
"Welcome to the newest chapter of the YRF Spy Universe — an edgy origin story of a girl raised and built to kill." — Yash Raj Films, official trailer

What makes the trailer crackle isn't just Bhatt, though. It's Sharvari. The Munjya breakout finally gets unleashed, and she is fierce, dangerous, and matches Bhatt punch for punch in combat sequences that are genuinely raw — two women throwing real, ugly, close-quarters blows, not the sanitised choreography the genre usually settles for. Sharvari has been saying for over a year that she wanted to be an action star. Watch ten seconds of this and you believe her.

Around them, the universe assembles. Anil Kapoor returns as Colonel Vikrant Kaul, R&AW chief, reprising his thread from War 2. And then the cameo that sent the fandom into a genuine frenzy: a blink-and-miss glimpse of Hrithik Roshan, allegedly back as Major Kabir Dhaliwal from War, cementing Alpha's place at the centre of the franchise rather than its margins. The crossover tease at the trailer's tail is the kind of move Marvel built an empire on, and YRF is now playing the same long game with a straight face.

!Bobby Deol — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

The aesthetic is darker and grimier than the glossy spy films before it — globe-trotting missions shot across Mumbai, Kashmir's Sonamarg and Pahalgam, and Valladolid in Spain, with cinematographer Rubais leaning into cold, steel-blue palettes over the usual sun-kissed sheen. This is a debut feature for director Shiv Rawail, who made his name on the acclaimed Netflix series The Railway Men, and he directs the action like someone with something to prove.

Off-screen, Bhatt has been generous about her co-stars, especially the much-discussed "new Bobby Deol" phase. "I had an amazing time working with him because he remains like a student in this cinematic journey even after so many years," she said, calling Deol a gentle giant who is "delivering one remarkable performance after another." The mentor-turned-adversary dynamic between them is the trailer's emotional spine, and on this evidence it earns its weight.

Of course, Alpha walked in carrying baggage. A loud section of the internet had decided to dislike it before a single frame existed — partly the reflexive trolling that trails Bhatt's every release, partly the franchise's own polarising politics. But the noise has done little. The trailer's momentum suggests the film has cut through, and the appetite for a female-led blockbuster of this scale feels real rather than manufactured.

For the diaspora, the date to circle is July 3, 2026, when Alpha releases in theatres worldwide in Hindi — expect wide releases across the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf through the usual YRF international network, with subtitled showings in most major markets. It arrives the same day as Huma Qureshi's Baby Do Die Do, setting up a rare double bill of desi women with body counts. After the streaming window, a YRF title of this size will almost certainly land on Amazon Prime Video, the franchise's recent home.

The teaser showed us the first kill. The trailer promised the hunt. If the full film delivers on even half of what these three minutes suggest, Bhatt and Sharvari won't just be guests in the Spy Universe — they'll be running it. Sita came to burn Lanka. We're watching.
